newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity continues plunge on unit returns.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity continues plunge on unit returns.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures continued to plunge Tuesday as traders looked for milder weather and the return of a number of power generation units in the U.S. West, industry sources said.

As of 1205 EDT, July Palo Verde was down $3.32 at $27.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $27.20-28.30, while August was down $2.90 at the day's low of $29.50 after peaking at $30.25 per MWh.
July California Oregon Border (COB) was down $3.60 at $17.50 after trades at $17.25-19.25, while August COB was $2.81 lower at $21.25 following trades in a range of $21.00-22.25 per MWh.
As of 1120 EDT, an estimated total of 186 COB and 250 PV contracts traded, NYMEX said.
The lower prices were seen as a combination of generation unit returns, lower physical power prices and mild weather in the West, sources said.
However, futures may have fallen enough to have found some strength at current levels, several of the sources said.
"Really, I think we've hit a floor here, there now seems to be some support," said one New York based futures trader.

Physical power prices were said to be weaker, with early quotes of firm, peak electricity at COB for Wednesday assessed at $15.50-16.50, down from $19.00-20.00 for today, while PV was pegged at $28.00-31.00, down from $42.00-43.00 for today.
The power complex was also under pressure Monday after Bonneville Power Administration slashed its next day peak firm power price by $12.00 per MWh to $19.00.

Two nuclear power units, the 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 and 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3, were boosting power early Tuesday following outages, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
A 750 MW unit at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico was expected to restart at midnight Tuesday, slightly behind its original schedule.
As of 1200, NYMEX July Henry Hub natgas futures were up two cents at $2.13 per million British thermal units.

Temperatures in the West were called to average near to slightly above normal into early next week with above normal precipitation in the eastern sections of the Northwest and northern areas of the Southwest.
